# Uṭṭhāna Sutta (Snp 2.10 (PTS Snp 57))
**ID:** Snp 2.10 (PTS Snp 57)
**Section:** Suttanipāta (snp)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-2
**Title (Pali):** Uṭṭhāna Sutta
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/snp2.10

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Uṭṭhāna Sutta* ("Get up! Make an Effort!") is the tenth discourse of the *Cūḷavagga*, the second chapter of the *Suttanipāta* (Snp 2.10, PTS Snp 57) [Hazra 1994; SuttaCentral]. Containing just four verses, it is one of the shortest didactic poems in the collection [Katre 1931]. The discourse delivers an urgent call to awake and practice: practitioners are exhorted to rise, sit, and train firmly for peace so that King Death (*maccurāja*) does not overpower them while negligent [Katre 1931; SuttaCentral]. Govind Chandra Pande notes that the text equates negligence (*pamāda*) to defilement or dust (*raja*) and vigorously advocates heedfulness (*appamāda*) [Pande 1974]. Comparing early Buddhist verse with Upanishadic literature, S. M. Katre observes that the sutta's opening refrain (*Uṭṭhahatha nisīdatha...*) directly echoes the well-known exhortation to arise and awake found in *Kaṭha Upaniṣad* 3.14 (*uttiṣṭhata jāgrata...*) [Katre 1931]. In nineteenth-century scholarship, T. W. Rhys Davids cited the sutta in his treatments of early Buddhist doctrine [Harris 2006].
SuttaCentral identifies a direct passage-level parallel in the *Theragāthā* (Thag 6.5, the *Mālukyaputtattheragāthā*) [SuttaCentral]. Resembling verses and shared imagery appear widely in early verse corpora, including the Pali *Dhammapada* (Dhp 315), the Gāndhārī Dharmapada (*Magavagga*, G-Dhp 97–134), the Patna Dharmapada (*Śaraṇavagga*, P-Dhp 216–238), the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* (UV 5, Priyavarga), Chinese verse parallels (T 210, T 212, T 213), *Aṅguttara Nikāya* 8.29 (*Akkhaṇasutta*), Thag 14.1, Thag 17.2, and *Therīgāthā* 1.5 [Barua 1921; SuttaCentral]. In addition, DharmaNexus identifies machine text-reuse matches between this sutta and the Tibetan version of the *Ārya-saddharmānusmṛtyupasthāna* (D0287-2) [DharmaNexus].
